summary: Browser iframe-injection payload shipped as an npm package
details: The main entry px.js is a self-executing browser-DOM script that creates a full-viewport iframe pointing at the hardcoded remote URL https://mfmz.hmbcfv.cn/H.html?c=0gjr with a Chinese loading overlay, using document.write / document.createElement / document.body.appendChild. There are no npm lifecycle scripts, no Node-side network I/O, no credential or environment reads, and no shell execution. Loading the module in Node throws because `document` is undefined, so `npm install` and `require()` in a Node context do not run the payload. The behavior only materializes if a downstream web project bundles px.js into a page delivered to browsers, in which case end users of that page are redirected into the remote iframe. The remote page content is author-controlled and mutable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
